articles.title: Upper Commons Gets $25,000 for Streetlight Upgrade
articles.deck: Residents of Upper Commons filled the hall on Wednesday to ask questions about the plan.
body: Albert Ingersoll, who has lived in Upper Commons for 35 years, said the response has been better than anyone expected.
Organizers say the project is on schedule and that volunteers are still needed on Wednesday mornings. The Upper Commons Improvement Group will post updates on its bulletin board outside the library.
Public works estimates the work will take about 35 weeks once it begins. The group has raised $25,000 so far and is asking for help with supplies and food.

articles.title: Foundry Row Asks Council for Speed Limit Change
articles.deck: The vote came after 27 residents spoke at Thursday’s session.
body: Staff recommended approval with two conditions: a traffic study and a public notice period of 30 days.
Public works estimates the work will take about 27 weeks once it starts in March.

Residents of Foundry Row said they had been asking for action for years, and several brought photographs of the street. Councilmember Janet Kellerman asked for more time to review the proposal, which would cost about $25,000.

articles.title: Millrace High School Board Approves Pocket Park
articles.deck: The program begins in April and is open to all students in grade 5 and up.
body: Principal Talia Dunmore said the program was built with help from parents and local volunteers. Sign-up forms went home in backpacks this week, and the first session is set for April.
Students will meet on Monday afternoons in the Millrace library, and transportation will be provided for those who need it.

articles.title: Owen Kozak, 95, Longtime Volunteer
articles.deck: Friends remember Owen Kozak for the many years of service to Tannery Flats.
body: Owen Kozak died in September at home on Rail Road, at the age of 95. Services will be held at the parish hall, and donations may be made to the Eastgate Senior Lunch Program in his or her name.

Survivors include a daughter, two grandchildren and many friends from Tannery Flats. Born in Tannery Flats in the years after the war, Owen Kozak spent most of a working life in the trades and most of a retirement in the neighborhood.
